note: The two sets are nearly identical in content and share the same core defects: contradictory duplicate readings at the same span station (mass density 3000 vs 3100, axial 4.5e10 vs 4.7e10, torsional 0.8e11 vs 0.9e11, edge 1.4e11 vs 1.5e11 at r/R=0), planform outline values misbound to the geometric/shear centers, and quotes that are only axis labels. Set B adds one further unsupported claim (mass density 0 kg/m at r/R=1.0, contradicting its own 100 kg/m claim and the plotted curve) plus an extra repeat of the axial-stiffness-zero claim. Set A therefore carries fewer wrong claims while keeping the same correct content, so it is marginally better.
remarks: Both sets read values off plotted curves, so several numbers are only approximate; the pairs of conflicting values at r/R=0 (3000/3100, 4.5e10/4.7e10, 0.8e11/0.9e11, 1.4e11/1.5e11) look like two independent extractions of the same point, one of which is wrong in each pair. The claims of exactly 0 stiffness/density at r/R=1.0 are also questionable since the curves end slightly above zero. Both sets bind the planform outline extremes (2 m, -4 m, -3 m) to the geometric and shear centers rather than to the blade surface, and both omit the fact that the properties were computed using PreComp. Quotes throughout are axis/legend labels and do not substantiate the numeric values.
